title: Learning New Categories from Handfuls of Labelled Images
abstract: We study how a classifier can acquire previously unseen categories when only a handful of labelled images per class are available. A meta-trained prototype network adapts rapidly and outperforms fine-tuning baselines.

title: Episodic Meta-Training for Low-Data Recognition
abstract: Models are trained across many small tasks so that adaptation to a novel task needs only a few gradient steps. Experiments show strong generalisation when supervision is extremely scarce.

title: Metric Spaces for Data-Scarce Classification
abstract: We learn an embedding where distance to a support set of a few examples determines class membership. The method reaches high accuracy with one to five samples per category.

title: Transferring Knowledge to Rare Classes
abstract: Rare categories with very few training instances are hard for deep networks. We propose feature hallucination that augments minority classes and improves recognition.

title: Message Passing on Relational Structures
abstract: We propose a neural architecture that aggregates information from neighbouring nodes in a network to produce node representations. It achieves strong results on citation and social network benchmarks.

title: Spectral Convolutions over Irregular Domains
abstract: Convolution is generalised to data defined on nodes and edges using the eigenbasis of the graph Laplacian. The approach classifies vertices with limited labels.

title: Attention Mechanisms for Networked Data
abstract: A learned attention weight is assigned to each neighbour of a vertex so that more informative connections dominate aggregation. Accuracy improves on molecular and citation graphs.

title: Predicting Links in Large Interaction Networks
abstract: We embed entities and their relations to forecast missing edges in knowledge bases and social platforms using stacked neighbourhood aggregation.

title: Predicting Three-Dimensional Folds from Amino Acid Sequences
abstract: A deep network infers the spatial arrangement of residues directly from the sequence of a polypeptide chain. Predicted structures approach experimental accuracy.

title: Co-evolution Signals for Residue Contact Estimation
abstract: Correlated mutations across homologous families reveal which residues are close in space. We use these signals to estimate tertiary structure of biomolecules.

title: Neural Models of Biomolecular Geometry
abstract: We design an equivariant architecture that reasons about atomic coordinates and outputs the native conformation of macromolecules, accelerating drug discovery.

title: Language Models Trained on Evolutionary Sequence Data
abstract: Self-supervised pretraining on millions of protein sequences yields representations that capture structure and function without alignments.

title: Attention-Based Sequence Models for Cross-Lingual Text Conversion
abstract: We present an encoder-decoder system that converts sentences from one human language into another using learned alignment. It yields higher BLEU than phrase-based systems.

title: Translating Between Languages Without Parallel Corpora
abstract: Unsupervised methods map monolingual embeddings of two languages into a shared space, enabling sentence conversion with no aligned examples.

title: Subword Units for Open-Vocabulary Language Conversion
abstract: Rare and unseen words are handled by splitting them into smaller units, improving the rendering of morphologically rich languages.

title: Multilingual Pretraining for Low-Resource Language Pairs
abstract: A single model trained on many languages transfers to pairs with little bilingual text, raising output quality for under-resourced languages.

title: Pixel-Wise Labelling of Street Scenes
abstract: A fully convolutional architecture assigns a semantic class to every pixel in an urban image, delineating roads, vehicles and pedestrians.

title: Delineating Organs in Volumetric Medical Scans
abstract: An encoder-decoder with skip connections outlines anatomical structures in tomography volumes, supporting radiotherapy planning with limited annotated data.

title: Instance Masks with Region Proposals
abstract: We extend a detection framework to predict a binary mask for each object, separating overlapping items in cluttered photographs.

title: Boundary-Aware Partitioning of Satellite Imagery
abstract: Land-cover regions are partitioned into coherent segments using boundary refinement, improving mapping of fields and buildings from aerial views.

title: Learning Control Policies through Trial and Error
abstract: An agent improves its decision rule by interacting with an environment and maximising cumulative reward. We demonstrate mastery of arcade games from raw pixels.

title: Value Estimation with Deep Function Approximators
abstract: A neural network approximates expected return for each action, stabilised by replay of past experience and slowly updated target networks.

title: Policy Gradient Methods with Trust Regions
abstract: We constrain each update of a stochastic policy to remain close to the previous one, achieving reliable improvement on locomotion tasks.

title: Exploration Bonuses for Sparse-Reward Environments
abstract: Curiosity-driven intrinsic signals encourage an agent to visit novel states when external feedback is rare, solving hard-exploration problems.

title: Training Models Across Decentralised Devices
abstract: Many phones jointly train a shared model while raw user data stays on each device; only parameter updates are averaged by a coordinating server.

title: Protecting Individuals in Collaborative Learning
abstract: We add calibrated noise to gradients so that no single person's record can be inferred from a released model, giving formal privacy guarantees.

title: Communication-Efficient Distributed Optimisation
abstract: Compressing and sparsifying updates reduces bandwidth when thousands of clients with heterogeneous data take part in training.

title: Secure Aggregation without Revealing Individual Contributions
abstract: Cryptographic masking lets a server compute the sum of client updates without seeing any single one, safeguarding confidential information.

title: End-to-End Transcription of Spoken Utterances
abstract: A single neural network maps acoustic waveforms directly to text without a hand-built pronunciation lexicon, lowering word error rate on conversational audio.

title: Self-Supervised Representations of Raw Audio
abstract: Pretraining on unlabelled recordings yields features that make recognising spoken words possible with only a few hours of transcribed data.

title: Robust Recognition of Speech in Noisy Environments
abstract: Data augmentation and enhancement front-ends improve transcription accuracy when background noise and reverberation corrupt the signal.

title: Streaming Decoding for Voice Assistants
abstract: A low-latency model converts speech to text incrementally as the user talks, enabling responsive voice interfaces on mobile hardware.
